subject: Triggered rollback language and channel-margin guardrails for private offer
messages:
From: Maya Patel <procurement@clearwave.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@resellco.io>
Date: Sat, 4 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer triggers + channel margin question

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the Clearwave team is excited about Redwood's performance on the vision pipelines. Procurement is starting to stitch together the private offer with our Finance and Channel ops teams. Before we surface the PO internally we have two points we need clarity on so we can confirm the economics to our reseller partner: 

1) Triggered rollback language: if our usage falls 30% below the committed baseline for two consecutive quarters, what is the standard rollback mechanism you propose? Do you apply a price step-back, requirement to true-up, or both?

2) Channel margin handling: our reseller (ResellCo) needs an assurance on how the passback/commission behaves if list prices are rolled back due to low utilization. Specifically, will ResellCo's margin be preserved as a fixed percentage of total net, or is it a variable passback tied to list price anchors?

I've attached a draft PO to show the structure (Clearwave_PO_Draft_0304.pdf). Can you provide a short written response we can include in our internal vendor memo? Ideally by COB Monday.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Procurement Manager, Clearwave Systems

---
Attachment: Clearwave_PO_Draft_0304.pdf (pdf, 98KB)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <procurement@clearwave.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@resellco.io>
Date: Sat, 4 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer triggers + channel margin question

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear note. Quick response below and tagging Irene and Vanessa for channel/ops validation.

1) Triggered rollback: our recommended approach for a 30% sustained drop is a staged rollback paired with an option to true-up. Typical clause we propose: if average quarterly consumption falls >=30% of committed baseline for two consecutive quarters, Redwood and customer will agree to one of the following within 30 days:
  - Option A: reduce list price for remaining term by a negotiated step (e.g., 10–20%), keeping billing cadence and SKU structure the same; or
  - Option B: maintain list price but require a usage true-up to the committed baseline for that quarter (subject to customer right to provide forecast evidence).
We include a one-time adjustment window (30 days) to allow forecast corrections. Either path will be mutually agreed and documented as an amendment.

2) Channel margin / passback: short answer — we do not automatically rebench reseller margin when list price is stepped down; instead we provide a protected passback floor for a contracted period. Operationally we can do either: keep reseller margin as a fixed percent of net invoice, or treat margin as a dollar-per-unit residual tied to original list anchor. We typically recommend a 6–9 month protected margin period after any rollback (so ResellCo would see consistent economics), after which we reconcile based on the then-current list.

I'll leave the exact language and the model to Irene (pricing) and Vanessa (channel ops) — attaching a working draft of the private offer (az-private-offer-draft.pdf) and asking them to run margin scenarios against your PO.

Next steps: Irene/Vanessa — can you review the PO and push back any internal constraints (tax, reseller invoicing, or marketplace passback timing)? Maya — happy to hop on a 30-min call next week if it helps.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Head of Marketplace Deals | Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: az-private-offer-draft.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <procurement@clearwave.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@resellco.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Mar 2028 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer triggers + channel margin question

Thanks for the tag — ran a quick model against the PO and the scenarios below. Attaching the channel margin workbook (channel_margin_model.xlsx) with the three scenarios labeled.

Summary points:
- Preserved-margin window: we can commit to a protected reseller margin of the greater of (A) a fixed percentage of net invoice (e.g., 18% of net) or (B) a shadow-dollar floor derived from the original list for the first 6 months post-rollback. This covers ResellCo's go-to-market commitment and eases churn risk.
- Reconciliation cadence: after the protected window, a reconciliation will run quarterly to align passbacks with the then-current list price. Reconciliation will not be retroactive beyond the protected window.
- Mechanic for step-back: we prefer Option A (reduce list price by negotiated step) because Option B requires constant true-ups that complicate marketplace invoicing and can trigger chargebacks to the reseller. The draft clause I propose is included in the workbook comments.
- Invoice pathing: for AWS private offers we're constrained by Marketplace invoicing. For Azure, we can effect the change at the vendor-billing layer and preserve reseller passback as agreed. That means region/workload choice in the PO matters (please confirm target cloud).

Questions / asks for Clearwave and ResellCo:
1) Maya: confirm target cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure). If AWS, we need to map the invoicing flow that ResellCo expects.
2) Tom: can ResellCo accept a protected-dollar floor rather than a fixed percent for the 6-month window? The attached model shows coverages at 12%, 18%, and 22% fixed percent vs a $/node floor.

If everyone is aligned I can bake the exact wording into the PO and return a redline by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference

Irene / Lukas — thanks, that is really helpful and clears up a lot.

Confirming: target cloud for this deal is Azure (we prefer the vendor-billing path). Tom confirmed on his side that ResellCo can accept a protected-dollar floor for the first 6 months, after which you can reconcile to a percentage as you described. Can you prepare the redline with the protected-floor language and the 6-month timing?

Also — can you add a clause that any rollback step (Option A) requires 30 days advance notice to both Clearwave and ResellCo, and that ResellCo gets one unilateral pass-through invoice schedule to ensure their AR is not disturbed? We'll want that in the vendor memo.

If you can send the redline and a short summary that we can paste into our internal memo (Finance + Channel Ops) by Thursday COB, we'll be in a position to issue a formal PO the following week. If it's easier, let's do a 30-minute sync on Thursday at 10am PT.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Procurement Manager, Clearwave Systems
